title: Calibrating the Alarms: A Registry-Grounded, Human-Validated Measurement of Poisoning Detectors on 16,763 MCP Tool Descriptions
description: An ecosystem-wide measurement study of the public Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry: what fraction of public servers expose dangerous capabilities, and what fraction ship tool descriptions with patterns exploitable for tool poisoning. The release pairs a registry-grounded crawl and GitHub enrichment of 16,763 MCP tool descriptions with heuristic detector outputs, a stratified human-validation sample, instance-level adjudication, and live ASR/refusal experiments, plus scripts that re-derive every number quoted in the manuscript (claim ledger, reproducibility manifest, gate battery, and trial accounting). Detector outputs are candidates rather than verdicts, and reported precision is explicitly sample-scoped. This is the pre-paper snapshot (v1.0.0) prepared for DOI citation.
